report:
# Research Findings: CBD for Dravet Syndrome Seizures

The claim that add-on cannabidiol (CBD) reduces convulsive seizure frequency in children with Dravet syndrome is **well-supported by strong evidence**, not false.

## Key Evidence

**Pivotal randomized controlled trial (Devinsky et al., NEJM 2017):** In a double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 120 children and young adults with Dravet syndrome and drug-resistant seizures were randomized to receive CBD oral solution (up to 20 mg/kg/day) or placebo added to their existing regimen. Median convulsive seizure frequency dropped by 39% in the CBD group versus 13% with placebo — a statistically significant difference (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1611618).

**Replication in a second trial (JAMA Neurology, 2020):** A dose-ranging trial similarly found adjunctive CBD significantly reduced convulsive seizures versus placebo, reinforcing the original findings (https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamaneurology/fullarticle/2762458).

**Long-term follow-up (Epilepsia, 2018):** Open-label extension studies showed that long-term CBD treatment had an acceptable safety profile and produced sustained, clinically meaningful reductions in seizure frequency over time (https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/epi.14628).

**Regulatory confirmation:** Based on this trial evidence, the FDA approved Epidiolex (pharmaceutical-grade CBD) in 2018 specifically for Dravet syndrome and Lennox-Gastaut syndrome — the first cannabis-derived drug approved by the agency (https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-approvals-and-databases/drug-trials-snapshots-epidiolex).

## Caveats
CBD is not a cure and doesn't eliminate seizures entirely; effects are add-on reductions (not complete control), and side effects (somnolence, liver enzyme elevations, appetite changes) are common. Still, the core statistical finding—reduced seizure frequency versus placebo—is robust and replicated.

## Conclusion
Multiple independent, peer-reviewed randomized trials and FDA approval consistently support this claim. The evidence base is strong; the claim is **true**, not false.
